messages:
indra.patel: Heads up — I just found a ClusterRoleBinding called `gpu-access-aggregator` that grants broad impersonation to `system:serviceaccount:prod-apps:app-sa`. It appears to allow cross-namespace access into the gpu-pool namespace. :eyes:
alex.kim: ugh, can you paste the binding yaml?
maria.lopez: running quick checks now. on it.
indra.patel: pasted output from control-plane earlier (trimmed):
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-access-aggregator
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: gpu-adminish
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: app-sa
  namespace: prod-apps
```
alex.kim: that `gpu-adminish` clusterrole has aggregated rules that include `impersonate` on serviceaccounts? if so that's bad.
maria.lopez: quick cmd I ran: `kubectl get clusterrole gpu-adminish -o yaml` shows `- verbs: ["impersonate"]` for `serviceaccounts/token` and `pods/exec`.
indra.patel: yep. looks like a legacy aggregation rule from when we wanted cross-namespace admin for certain infra teams.
ranA.singh: (typo) rana.singh: we should remove the cluster-wide binding immediately and create a narrow namespaced Role for gpu-pool.
sre-bot: Alert: Unusual RBAC binding detected for serviceaccount prod-apps/app-sa (rule id RBAC-4721). Auto-notify sent to eng-security.
deply-bot: Deploys to gpu-pool are currently allowed but we'll pause any automated rollouts until this is resolved.
ciso-jane: Priority: high. Need audit evidence of which tokens were minted using that SA in the last 48h. If any long-lived tokens exist, rotate.
maria.lopez: query I ran against audit logs (gke):
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type=k8s_cluster AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="system:serviceaccount:prod-apps:app-sa"' --limit 100 --freshness=48h
```
maria.lopez: returned 7 token create events and 3 execs into gpu-pool nodes, timestamps within last 12h.
indra.patel: ok assign mitigation: immediate removal of clusterrolebinding, create a namespaced role limited to `get,list` on nodes/pods and a rolebinding scoped to a new SA if needed.
rana.singh: proposed fix (quick):
```bash
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding gpu-access-aggregator
kubectl create role gpu-access-ns --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods,nodes -n gpu-pool
kubectl create rolebinding app-sa-gpu -n gpu-pool --role=gpu-access-ns --serviceaccount=prod-apps:app-sa
```
rana.singh: after delete, I'll open a PR to convert the old aggregated clusterrole into explicit namespaced roles with docs.
alex.kim: before delete — can we put an admission hold with Gatekeeper to block impersonate verbs coming from cluster roles? I can push a short-term ConstraintTemplate + Constraint that denies `impersonate` in ClusterRole rules.
indra.patel: good idea. please DO that first so we have a quick guard while rana prepares the namespaced roles.
alex.kim: pushed Gatekeeper constraint (preview):
```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sDenyImpersonate
metadata:
  name: deny-impersonate-clusterroles
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```
alex.kim: that blocked a test create for the offending clusterrolebinding — verified. :white_check_mark:
maria.lopez: audit follow-up: I collected the container exec logs and started a list of affected pods, adding to the incident board.
ciso-jane: KMS question: were any service account keys or secrets egressed? we need to check KMS decrypt logs for the SA token key. If tokens were created client-side and encrypted, rotate the KMS key.
indra.patel: I've checked KMS audit — no decrypts from unknown principals, but I want to rotate the service-account token signing key as a precaution since there were execs.
rana.singh: rotation plan: short term — revoke existing tokens for app-sa, create a new SA with minimal roles and update deployments to use the new SA. Long term — remove cluster-level aggregation and add an RBAC lint step to CI.
alex.kim: I'll take the Gatekeeper PR and add the RBAC lint CI job (cheap scan that flags `impersonate` in clusterroles).
maria.lopez: I'm running token revocation now: `kubectl delete secret -n prod-apps $(kubectl get secret -n prod-apps -o name | grep app-sa-token)` then restart deployments that mount the SA token.
deply-bot: Can confirm: automated rollout paused for gpu-pool until `eng-security` clears.
ciso-jane: let's treat this as a vuln triage: severity=high, timeline created, owners=(rana, alex, maria). Create a follow-up ticket for postmortem and compliance evidence upload.
indra.patel: assigning owners as above. Rana — remap roles and PR. Alex — Gatekeeper + CI lint. Maria — audit artifacts + token rotation. I'll coordinate with infra to approve emergency changes.
rana.singh: will open PR in ~30m. marking as hotfix.
alex.kim: PR for Gatekeeper + CI lint posted, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/org/pull/4321 (tests passing locally).
maria.lopez: uploaded audit logs & exec transcripts to the incident doc. link: https://docs.internal/redwood/security/incidents/1912345678
ciso-jane: after remediation, we need evidence for SOC — show deleted clusterrolebinding, new namespaced rolebindings, KMS audit, and rotated token timestamps.
indra.patel: agreed. we'll keep this thread as the coordination log. thanks everyone for quick responses. :lock: :thumbsup:
alex.kim: small follow-up: add an integration test that simulates SA trying to impersonate another SA and ensure deny policy triggers. I'll add it to eng-infra tests.
maria.lopez: closing loop — sentinel alert will escalate if similar `impersonate` clusterrolebindings are created.
sre-bot: Incident RBAC-4721 moved to resolved state after applied mitigations and PR merges.
indra.patel: marking follow-ups in ticket and closing Slack thread in ~1h after postmortem doc review. Thanks.
